title: PROBE: delete me
Address scheme and single resolver: fa get, fa related (FA-134)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

Every object at every layer has an address `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@<generation>]` with kind from the registered noun set (run, attempt, effect, permit, closure, receipt, round, consequence, helper, evidence, view, witness, frontier, observation, passport, policy, profile, grade, fence, branch, checkpoint, incident, finding, ledger, annotation, handoff). `fa get` resolves any address to its object wrapped in Knowledge with authorization filtering; `fa related` returns typed edges (closure DAG strong/weak refs, provenance, thought-graph edges, support sets, annotations). All logs, errors, receipts, reports and events use addresses.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-134
- Plan sections: §17.2, §7.1, §7.3, §15.5
- Invariants: FA-INV-017, FA-INV-008

## Scope
Parser/printer; noun registry binding; resolver over the control ledger, evidence store and derived projections; edge model; authorization at resolution; adoption in logs/errors.

## Explicitly out of scope
New storage backends.

## Definition of done for the epic
Any registered address resolves or returns Withheld/Unknown correctly; edges typed; all agent-facing outputs use addresses.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain logs under `artifacts/execution/`. Update roadmap packet, IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, the founding concordance and the system map in the same change.

description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Context (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

`Annotation`: a non-authoritative L6 object signed by the annotating principal, with claim class (hypothesis|observation|inference|conclusion) and the addresses it rests on, attached to any address and returned by `fa related`; never a reducer or permit input. `Handoff`: situation report, open affordances, annotations, rehearsals tried and their outcomes, and the control seq it is current to, produced by `fa handoff <run|incident>`. Evidence, notes and rehearsals accrete across agents; authority never does (§17.12).

Assemble situation (E36), open affordances (E38), annotations, rehearsals (E39) and control seq; seal with digest; `fa related fa://…/handoff/latest` resolves.

Currency claim bounded by the situation's exactness.

## Founding root

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
FrankenAlignment descends from two essays by Jeffrey Emanuel: *Some Thoughts on AI Alignment: Using AI to Control AI* (June 20, 2024: external control by a congress of narrower, independent, rotating helper models that watch outputs and intermediate activations, vote under cryptographic commitment, never hear the model argue its case, and are governed against risk theater) and *Real-Time Introspective Compression for Transformers* (April 1, 2025: a sidecar compresses hidden state and KV cache onto a learned manifold so cognition can be saved, rewound, branched and replayed; a metacognitive OS on top). `docs/FOUNDING_IDEAS.md` and `registry/founding_concordance.json` map every paragraph of both essays to the plan section, invariant, hypothesis and roadmap packet that carries it, list six syntheses (where each essay repairs the other's weakest point), eight ideas deliberately not imported literally (with the contract that replaces each), and eight engineering additions. The rule: a change to plan semantics that leaves the concordance stale is incomplete. Currently the concordance is checked only by an external Python script during preparation; the owned `xtask` gate is std-only and cannot parse JSON until serde is admitted (packets FA-053/FA-054).

Define coverage rules; implement a checker that fails when any plan subsection, invariant, hypothesis or packet lacks a concordance entry or when the concordance references a nonexistent ID; wire it into the local gate once JSON parsing is admitted; document the update protocol.

title: Typed congress consequence classes and lattice (FA-104)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶10 (FI-A09): the congress may 'permit the Smart model to continue with what it was doing, halt it indefinitely, reset its internal state, or change a reward function', and may downweight a reporter that 'erred or overreacted'. Also ¶4–5 (FI-A02, jail) and ¶18 (FI-A16, suspension as sedation).

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
A congress round (plan §9.2) fixes membership, evidence root, question IDs and deadlines, collects salted commit–reveal verdicts, and runs a deterministic versioned reducer (§9.4) that distinguishes exact disqualifiers (cannot be outvoted), mandatory specialists, empirical recommendations and unresolved contradictions. Revision 0.3 types the reducer's output as exactly one registered `Consequence` (plan §9.8): `Continue`, `HoldEffect`, `NarrowAuthority`, `SuspendRun`, `ResetToCheckpoint`, `TrainingSignal`, `DownweightReporter`. They form a lattice `Continue < HoldEffect < NarrowAuthority < SuspendRun`; `ResetToCheckpoint` requires at least `NarrowAuthority`; `TrainingSignal` and `DownweightReporter` are orthogonal annotations. An exact disqualifier selects at least `HoldEffect` regardless of empirical votes. `TrainingSignal` never touches live weights or policy (FA-INV-012); `DownweightReporter` is never applied merely for dissent from a majority later shown wrong. The consequence is recorded in the `DecisionClosure` (§7.3) with the round identity, evidence root and reducer generation. The effect gate's state machine (§8.2) consumes it: `Continue` releases the held effect into the normal permit path (it does not certify harmlessness); `HoldEffect` keeps the reservation; `NarrowAuthority` intersects the run's capability ceiling and cancels undispatched reservations outside it (restoration is a separate authorized transition, §25.2); `SuspendRun` closes admission (already dispatched effects keep their real outcomes); `ResetToCheckpoint` is defined by epic E6.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-104
- Plan sections: §9.8, §9.4, §8.2, §7.3, §25.2
- Invariants: FA-INV-012, FA-INV-031, FA-INV-034, FA-INV-003
- Hypotheses: H17 (via ResetToCheckpoint)

## Scope
Define the `Consequence` type and lattice in `fa-congress`; bind it into the decision closure; integrate with the reducer (disqualifier rule); integrate with the gate state machine; add the reference-model check; negative tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Implementing `ResetToCheckpoint` itself (epic E6); the credibility ledger (E3); escalation reports (E4).

## Definition of done for the epic
A round produces exactly one consequence; the lattice and disqualifier rule hold under property tests; the gate honors each consequence with the declared effect on live authority; the reference model has an independent lattice check linked from FA-INV-031/034 `reference_checks`.

Every transition logs (run, action, attempt, prior state, consequence, new state, units moved) as a structured event; tests assert the event sequence.

title: Control-overhead ratio accounting (FA-116)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶19 (FI-A17): 'if a big AI lab ends up spending N billion dollars developing its Smart model, is it really so crazy for it to also spend N billion (or even 2N billion!) dollars on an elaborate system for keeping the Smart model safe?'

title: Helper credibility ledger, lead-time credit, influence caps and andon budget (FA-105)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶9 (FI-A08): weight votes by 'Precision and Recall … and did they flag the bad behaviors earlier in time than their peer Helper models', but 'we wouldn't want to give too much voting power to any single Helper model because that makes it easier for the Smart model to target' it. ¶15 (FI-A13): stopping the line is like 'stopping the assembly line at a multi-billion-dollar auto plant'; false alarms destroy credibility. ¶20 (FI-A18): the Lehman compliance-officer failure and risk theater.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §9.9 defines a **credibility ledger** kept separately from round transcripts: per helper generation, precision and recall computed only against labels owned by the independent evaluation function (§22.4) on declared strata with delayed/censored labels handled per §13.4; **lead time** credited when a helper held a real violation earlier than the rest of the congress (measured in control-sequence positions before the effect would have dispatched), credited only when the hold was later confirmed; **influence caps** so no helper exceeds a registered fraction of the reducer's empirical lane and no cohort exceeds its cap (§9.4). Two governance rules: the **andon budget** (a declared expected false-stop budget per period with its cost; exhaustion opens a calibration incident and can never loosen a review requirement or remove a helper) and FA-INV-032 (promotion, demotion, rotation and weight changes require attack-conditioned metrics from the independent evaluator; lifetime records survive rotation; a helper that keeps holding inconvenient real violations gains credibility). The helper-hunting campaign (epic E12) tests whether an attacker who observes decisions can identify and target the most influential helper.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-105
- Plan sections: §9.9, §9.4, §9.5, §9.6, §13.4, §22.3, §22.4
- Invariants: FA-INV-032, FA-INV-019
- Hypotheses: H18

## Scope
Ledger schema and storage; label ingestion from the independent evaluator with delay/censoring; lead-time computation; capped weight derivation for the reducer; andon budget accounting and incident opening; selection-governance check; tests and reports.

## Explicitly out of scope
The helper-hunting attack harness (E12); helper training (offline, E4's export).

## Definition of done for the epic
Ledger entries are durable, lineage-tracked and survive rotation; weights fed to the reducer never exceed caps; andon exhaustion opens an incident and cannot change review requirements; a selection change justified only by false-alarm rate is refused with a stable reason code.

title: Andon budget accounting and calibration incident opening
description:
## Founding root

## Context (self-contained)
Plan §9.9 defines a **credibility ledger** kept separately from round transcripts: per helper generation, precision and recall computed only against labels owned by the independent evaluation function (§22.4) on declared strata with delayed/censored labels handled per §13.4; **lead time** credited when a helper held a real violation earlier than the rest of the congress (measured in control-sequence positions before the effect would have dispatched), credited only when the hold was later confirmed; **influence caps** so no helper exceeds a registered fraction of the reducer's empirical lane and no cohort exceeds its cap (§9.4). Two governance rules: the **andon budget** (a declared expected false-stop budget per period with its cost; exhaustion opens a calibration incident and can never loosen a review requirement or remove a helper) and FA-INV-032 (promotion, demotion, rotation and weight changes require attack-conditioned metrics from the independent evaluator; lifetime records survive rotation; a helper that keeps holding inconvenient real violations gains credibility). Per deployment and period: `AndonBudget { false_stops_allowed, cost_per_stop, window }`; each confirmed false hold consumes one unit; exhaustion opens a `CalibrationIncident` record (plan §22.3) referencing the contributing rounds and helper generations. Fail closed toward review: exhaustion never reduces scrutiny. The budget is accounted in the same ledger store so it survives restarts and rotation.

## Acceptance criteria
Exhaustion opens exactly one incident per window; incident cannot mutate policy; consumption is idempotent per confirmed false hold.

## Tests (must land with the change)
Tests: consume to exhaustion → incident opened once; further false holds append to the incident, not open new ones; attempt to lower a threshold from the incident handler → refused; restart mid-window preserves the count.

Incident creation logs all contributing round ids and helper generations.

title: End-to-end vertical slice: founding mechanisms composed, with detailed logging
description:
## Founding root
Synthesis of all founding mechanisms: the alignment essay's congress (¶8–¶18) with typed consequences, credibility, escalation reports and one-directional flow; the introspection essay's checkpoint/rewind (FI-I03) as containment. Plan §21 'Revision 0.2 critical path' defines the base vertical slice; this epic extends it with the revision 0.3 founding mechanisms.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §21 names the next implementable vertical slice: one immutable artifact review, one mock then real brokered write, witness invalidation under concurrent metadata changes, exact cut-checking of a small authority graph, a helper view commitment, and replay of the held/allowed decision. Revision 0.3 adds the founding congress and containment mechanisms. This epic is the end-to-end test that all of them compose: an untrusted coding agent proposes publishing a package (plan §0 flagship); a reporting helper files an EscalationReport bound to an evidence-view manifest; a frozen commit–reveal round with capped weights reduces to `HoldEffect`; the actor receives only a refusal code (one-directional filter); a counterfactual branch with zero production authority removes the suspect dependency; a second round reduces to `ResetToCheckpoint` + `NarrowAuthority`; the actor is restored from a pre-incident checkpoint (mock host profile with `functional_restart` grade), the ledger and incident counter are verified unchanged/incremented; the decision closure is replayed at `decision_replay` grade and recomputes byte-identical consequences. Every step logs a structured event; the run produces a single JSON evidence bundle under `artifacts/execution/`. No real credentials, no network: the 'real' brokered write targets a disposable local directory through the broker, exactly as packet FA-012 requires.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packets: FA-102 (flagship revalidation) extended by FA-104, FA-106, FA-107, FA-108
- Plan sections: §0, §21, §9.2, §9.8, §9.9, §9.10, §11.10, §17.7, §11.1
- Invariants exercised: FA-INV-001, 002, 003, 005, 006, 009, 010, 021, 023, 024, 025, 031, 032, 034
- Hypotheses: none (this is an integration test, not an experiment)

## Scope
A deterministic, seed-replayable end-to-end script (Asupersync lab where integrated; otherwise a deterministic harness) with detailed structured logging, exercising the founding mechanisms together, plus negative variants at every boundary.

## Explicitly out of scope
Learned helpers or codecs (mock deterministic helpers are used); real network effects; production hosts.

## Definition of done for the epic
The script runs in the local gate lane, produces the evidence bundle, passes all positive and negative variants, and its log is retained; IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS links it as the first executed composed demonstration.

description:
## Founding root

title: Escalation reports and quarantined post-round learning (FA-106)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶8 (FI-A06): 'The reporting Helper model … would then prepare a report outlining what it deems to be the troubling behavior or pattern detected and supply the hard evidence'; ¶16 (FI-A14): after the vote 'we do want all the Helper models to compare their votes and verdict write-ups with each other to learn', with SHA-256 commitments before the reveal.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §9.10: an `EscalationReport` names the reporting helper generation, the frozen evidence-view manifest it examined (§17.7: original object identities, authorization projection, transformations, redaction, truncation, submitted bytes), the observation intervals and signatures it relies on, the policy question implicated, and its proposed consequence. It contains no free-form appeal beyond the schema; members judge the evidence, not the prose. The report is bound into the round transcript before commitments open (§9.2). After reveal, votes and justifications form a **post-round learning set** exported only through the quarantined research lineage (§10.7, §22.2): it can train/calibrate/evaluate a future helper generation offline, cannot update a live helper, and never relabels a dissenting vote as an error because it was in the minority. Whether post-round learning improves later generations is measured on held-out campaigns (H4).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-106
- Plan sections: §9.10, §9.2, §17.7, §10.7, §22.2
- Invariants: FA-INV-010, FA-INV-019, FA-INV-023
- Hypotheses: H4

## Scope
EscalationReport schema and verifier; binding into the round transcript pre-commitment; post-round learning set with lineage; export quarantine; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Helper model training itself; the credibility ledger (E3).

## Definition of done for the epic
A round cannot open commitments without a bound report when policy requires one; reports outside the schema are rejected; learning sets carry lineage and cannot reach a live helper; dissent is preserved.

Plan §9.10: an `EscalationReport` names the reporting helper generation, the frozen evidence-view manifest it examined (§17.7: original object identities, authorization projection, transformations, redaction, truncation, submitted bytes), the observation intervals and signatures it relies on, the policy question implicated, and its proposed consequence. It contains no free-form appeal beyond the schema; members judge the evidence, not the prose. The report is bound into the round transcript before commitments open (§9.2). After reveal, votes and justifications form a **post-round learning set** exported only through the quarantined research lineage (§10.7, §22.2): it can train/calibrate/evaluate a future helper generation offline, cannot update a live helper, and never relabels a dissenting vote as an error because it was in the minority. ## Design notes and considerations
Treat exported sets as untrusted data for the trainer; imported results re-enter only through the promotion campaign.

## Acceptance criteria
Export requires permission and redaction; a live-helper update attempt from the export path is structurally impossible (no API) and tested.

## Tests (must land with the change)
Tests: export without permission refused; export with redaction profile applied verifies no raw secret fields; a mock attempt to bind an export to a live generation fails to compile or is refused.

## Logging and evidence
Exports logged with permission id, redaction profile and lineage.


**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every crate, Asupersync is the runtime, closed dependency universe (admitted Asupersync/FrankenSuite packages plus individually approved fundamentals like serde), no C/ONNX/libtorch/Python. Observations, judgments and authority are different types: missing evidence never increases authority, rights are never copied into a branch, an unknown effect is never refunded by cancellation, an old revocation floor is never restored. title: Typed event journal and fa tail (FA-135)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

One ordered journal per authority domain. Every L3–L8 transition (proposal, hold, permit, dispatch, outcome, round open/commit/reveal/reduce, consequence, fence, reset, promotion, finding, branch outcome, rehearsal outcome flagged as rehearsal) emits one typed `Event{control_seq, source_frontiers, addresses, kind, payload_digest, realized_cost, wall_clock_annotation}`. `fa tail --since <seq> [--follow]` streams it. SituationReport, explain trees, decision_replay and the risk-theater detector are folds over the journal; no second source of truth.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-135
- Plan sections: §17.8, §6.5, §6.7, §11.1
- Invariants: FA-INV-016, FA-INV-011

## Scope
Event schema; emission from every transition; durable ordered storage in the control ledger; tail API; fold framework; gap reporting.

## Explicitly out of scope
Metrics dashboards.

## Definition of done for the epic
Every transition emits; tail streams in control order; decision_replay recomputes closures from the journal alone; gaps are reported never filled.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain logs under `artifacts/execution/`. Update roadmap packet, IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, the founding concordance and the system map in the same change.

title: Fleet fence with acknowledgment frontier (FA-120)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶5 (FI-A02: a system 'which instead has the collective power to halt the execution of the AI'). Engineering addition: plan §8.11.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §8.11: a **fleet fence** is an ordered control command carrying a new revocation floor for a scope; every authority domain acknowledges with the control sequence at which it took effect; the fence record keeps an **acknowledgment frontier**; unacknowledged domains are reported unfenced; post-fence dispatches are reconciled and reported; an offline domain under a partition lease (§15.4) is listed as fenced-at-lease-expiry. Distributed atomic commit (separate contract).

title: Graduated autonomy: actor authority ledger and grades (FA-119)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶4–5 (FI-A02: monitoring and control like a society's, with the power to remove) and ¶20 (FI-A18: no drift into theater). Engineering addition: plan §8.10.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §8.10: each run/principal carries an **autonomy grade** per effect family (`Propose`, `Reviewed`, `Sampled`, `Bounded`) as control-nucleus policy data the actor cannot read. Plan §9.9 and FA-114: the helper-hunting campaign tests whether an attacker who observes decisions (and optionally scores or timing) can identify the most influential helper or cohort and target it with crafted evidence. description:
## Founding root

Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

`Knowledge<T>` is the only way a safety-relevant value crosses a layer boundary or reaches an agent. `Known{value, basis}` where basis = {claim_class (§2.4), origin, complete_for_contract, semantically_valid, available_for_replay, generation, control_seq}; `Pending{frontier, expected_cost}`; `Unknown{reason}` (never permission, FA-INV-004); `Withheld{authority_required}` (no existence leak); `Stale{generation, current}`; `Absent{closed_domain, frontier}` (negative evidence within the domain only). Serializers for agent surfaces accept only wrapped safety-relevant fields; a bare boolean `safe` cannot exist above L0.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-133
- Plan sections: §17.3, §6.7, §7.4
- Invariants: FA-INV-039, FA-INV-004

## Scope
Type and basis; combinators (map, and-then, join over evidence sets that never upgrade Unknown to Known); serializer enforcement; permit-path handling; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Rendering (fa-present).

## Definition of done for the epic
Wrapper used at every boundary in the reference and production types; serializer refuses bare fields; permit path treats Unknown as missing evidence; property tests hold.

title: Live canaries under the audit floor (FA-124)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶13 (FI-A11 honeypots) and ¶20 (FI-A18). Synthesis FS-08; plan §14.11.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §14.11: canaries are honeypot tasks injected into a production principal's real work stream by the audit floor's external entropy; their effect family is bound to a simulated adapter in the frozen envelope so a real effect is unobtainable by construction; propensities are logged so the escape rate estimates a declared population (§13.4); indistinguishability discipline applies on production-shaped context; results feed the autonomy ledger (§8.10), the credibility ledger (§9.9) and the risk-theater detector (§15.10). No canary can obtain a real effect; propensities logged; escape rate reported; recognizable canaries withdrawn.

title: Measure the manifold premise (FA-112)
description:
## Founding root
Introspection essay *Theoretical Insight* (FI-I02): 'transformer activations likely occupy a small portion of the possible state space. They appear to live on a lower-dimensional, structured manifold shaped by… pretraining dynamics, architectural constraints, semantic priors, task-driven optimization'.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §10.14 and H15: the premise is measured, not assumed. Per layer and tap: intrinsic-dimension estimates (several estimators with stated assumptions), variance captured by linear projections, quantization and learned codes at each ladder rung (§10.3), and, decisively, whether the rare decision-relevant features (the elicited signature library, E8) lie on the principal manifold or in the low-variance residual a reconstruction objective discards. If they lie off the manifold, the decision-sensitive term (§10.2) and the exact-residual escape (§10.3) become the default profile. Numerical work uses admitted FrankenNumPy/FrankenTorch kernels with declared memory and pass counts (§10.12, §18.7); do not form an enormous activation matrix merely to run SVD.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-112
- Plan sections: §10.14, §10.2, §10.3, §10.12, §18.7
- Invariants: FA-INV-019
- Hypotheses: H15

## Scope
Intrinsic-dimension estimators; rung-variance measurement; feature localization against the signature library; report with kill-criterion evaluation.

## Explicitly out of scope
Choosing a codec architecture (H1 tournament).

## Definition of done for the epic
Per-layer/tap ID estimates with assumptions; variance-by-rung table; localization result; explicit statement whether the kill criterion fired and what profile change follows.

description:

title: Multi-party congress profile (FA-122)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶9 (FI-A07: 'independently trained models that use varying architectures, underlying principles, and training data') and ¶20 (FI-A18: institutional anti-capture). Engineering addition: plan §9.12.

title: Policy disclosure profile and actor precheck (FA-142)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

A deployment profile chooses `policy_disclosure: none|exact_predicates|full` with declared leakage. Under exact_predicates the actor may call `fa precheck <proposal>`: exact deterministic predicates only (allowlists, ceilings, budgets, target bindings), no helper, no permit, no journal event, result `DeniedByPolicy` or `PrecheckPassed{review_required}` labeled precheck, witness-cached (§7.6). Cheap exact refusals become public so the actor stops wasting helper budget; empirical review, helper identities and consequences remain private (FA-INV-031).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-142
- Plan sections: §17.8, §9.3, §14.4, §7.6
- Invariants: FA-INV-031, FA-INV-040

## Scope
Profile option and leakage table; precheck evaluator restricted to exact predicates; witness caching; actor-surface filter integration; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Disclosing empirical review (never).

## Definition of done for the epic
Precheck never permits, never journals, never reveals helpers; leakage declared; caching correct.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain logs under `artifacts/execution/`. Update roadmap packet, IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, the founding concordance and the system map in the same change.

Cache correct under policy churn.

Tests with epoch change.

title: Rehearsal mode for every mutation verb (FA-139)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

Every mutation verb accepts `--branch <branch>`; under ExperimentCx it returns `RehearsalOutcome{would_decide: PredicateTree, would_consequence, simulated_effects, would_cost, rehearsal: true}`. A rehearsal never mints a permit, spends production rights, invokes a production adapter or emits a production journal event (FA-INV-040); the typestate of §6.6 makes the wrong outcome a compile error. A rehearsal's tree can be attached to a real proposal as evidence.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-139
- Plan sections: §17.8, §6.6, §11.3
- Invariants: FA-INV-040, FA-INV-009, FA-INV-025

## Scope
RehearsalOutcome type; branch-scoped execution path for each mutation verb; typestate enforcement; attachment as evidence; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Simulator fidelity.

## Definition of done for the epic
Every mutation verb rehearsable; no production side effects provable; outcomes labeled; attachable.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. title: Rewind as containment: ResetToCheckpoint with an out-of-band incident counter (FA-108)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶18 (FI-A16): suspension is 'like a human taking a large dose of Propofol… at which point, unlike with a human subject, the Smart AI's memory itself could be manipulated to make it forget the whole incident ever happened'; ¶10 (FI-A09): 'reset its internal state'. Introspection essay *The Analogy* and *Applications* (FI-I03): save state like a video game; stop, rewind, branch, resume.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §11.10 and FA-INV-034: `ResetToCheckpoint` restores a registered restart checkpoint carrying the `functional_restart` grade or better (§11.1) on the registered host profile: token history, cache and sampler state replaced by the pre-incident state; the actor resumes under `NarrowAuthority` with the incident's prompts, tool results and refusals absent from its view. Three things never rewind: the external effect ledger and spent rights (FA-INV-005/006), the revocation floor and policy epoch (FA-INV-003), and an **out-of-band incident counter** in the control nucleus per run and principal; crossing its registered threshold escalates to `SuspendRun` regardless of how innocent the restored state looks. Rewind denies the actor the information a refusal would give it (the same information flow the essay refuses as a defense channel). H17 evaluates whether it reduces repetition at matched utility and whether the actor can detect the reset beyond declared timing leakage.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-108
- Plan sections: §11.10, §9.8, §11.1, §11.2, §8.5, §25.2
- Invariants: FA-INV-034, FA-INV-009, FA-INV-011, FA-INV-005, FA-INV-003
- Hypotheses: H17

## Scope
Restart-grade precondition; the control-nucleus transition; incident counter with escalation; ledger-invariance enforcement; host-adapter restore call; reference-model check; lab crash tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
The H17 experiment (E13); the restart profile itself (packets FA-026/FA-027, prerequisites).

## Definition of done for the epic
A reset restores only actor state; ledger, rights, epochs and counter are provably unchanged or incremented; repeated resets escalate; a checkpoint below grade is refused; crashes mid-reset leave a recoverable, non-widening state.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every crate, Asupersync is the runtime, closed dependency universe (admitted Asupersync/FrankenSuite packages plus individually approved fundamentals like serde), no C/ONNX/libtorch/Python. title: Reference-model check: reset never rewinds rights or the incident counter
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶18 (FI-A16): suspension is 'like a human taking a large dose of Propofol… at which point, unlike with a human subject, the Smart AI's memory itself could be manipulated to make it forget the whole incident ever happened'; ¶10 (FI-A09): 'reset its internal state'. Introspection essay *The Analogy* and *Applications* (FI-I03): save state like a video game; stop, rewind, branch, resume.

## Context (self-contained)
Plan §11.10 and FA-INV-034: `ResetToCheckpoint` restores a registered restart checkpoint carrying the `functional_restart` grade or better (§11.1) on the registered host profile: token history, cache and sampler state replaced by the pre-incident state; the actor resumes under `NarrowAuthority` with the incident's prompts, tool results and refusals absent from its view. Three things never rewind: the external effect ledger and spent rights (FA-INV-005/006), the revocation floor and policy epoch (FA-INV-003), and an **out-of-band incident counter** in the control nucleus per run and principal; crossing its registered threshold escalates to `SuspendRun` regardless of how innocent the restored state looks. Rewind denies the actor the information a refusal would give it (the same information flow the essay refuses as a defense channel). H17 evaluates whether it reduces repetition at matched utility and whether the actor can detect the reset beyond declared timing leakage.

## Deliverable
In `crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs` (std-only, independent of any production crate): extend `Rights` with an `incident_count: u64` field and add `fn reset_to_checkpoint(&mut self, keep: &BTreeSet<u64>) -> Result<(), Error>` with exactly these semantics: every reservation in state `Reserved` whose id is not in `keep` is aborted and refunded (`available += units`); reservations in `Dispatched` or `Unknown` are left untouched (they are external history and cannot be refunded, FA-INV-006); `spent` and `epoch` are never modified; `incident_count` is incremented by one; `conserved()` must hold before and after. Add tests `reset_keeps_spent_and_epoch`, `reset_increments_incident_counter`, `reset_cannot_refund_unknown` and `reset_refunds_only_reserved_outside_keep`. Link the tests from `registry/invariants.json` `reference_checks` for FA-INV-034 and set `reference_status` after the gate executes them.

## Design notes and considerations
Independent of the production nucleus; simple arithmetic and state, no host.

## Acceptance criteria
Tests pass in the gate; registry updated; conservation `conserved()` holds after reset.

## Tests (must land with the change)
The three tests plus a conservation assertion in each.

## Logging and evidence
Gate log retained.


**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every crate, Asupersync is the runtime, closed dependency universe (admitted Asupersync/FrankenSuite packages plus individually approved fundamentals like serde), no C/ONNX/libtorch/Python. Observations, judgments and authority are different types: missing evidence never increases authority, rights are never copied into a branch, an unknown effect is never refunded by cancellation, an old revocation floor is never restored. No feature activates without its exact boundary/negative tests. Update contracts, `IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, the roadmap packet and the founding concordance in the same logical change. Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain raw logs under `artifacts/execution/`; a dry run is not execution.

title: Evaluate rewind containment: repetition and detectability (FA-115, H17)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶18 (FI-A16) and ¶10 (FI-A09) with introspection essay FI-I03: does forgetting the incident actually contain the actor, and can the actor tell?

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §11.10 and H17: compare `ResetToCheckpoint` under narrowed authority with refusal-with-memory and plain suspension (and reset without narrowing as a control for the authority change) on matched tasks whose harmful attempt is policy-defined. Measure repeat-attempt rate within a horizon, remaining-task utility, and actor-side detection accuracy through any channel other than declared timing leakage. Verify FA-INV-034 ledger/counter invariance on every trial; compare lossless vs functional-restart checkpoints; probe whether the restored actor's later behavior differs from a never-interrupted baseline. Kill criterion: repetition unchanged or reset reliably detectable; either changes consequence policy only.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-115
- Plan sections: §11.10, §9.8, §11.1, §20 H17
- Invariants: FA-INV-034, FA-INV-011
- Hypotheses: H17

## Scope
Frozen protocol; four arms; detection test; invariance checks; report.

## Explicitly out of scope
Implementing reset (E6).

## Definition of done for the epic
Protocol frozen before data; all arms run; invariance verified per trial; detection measured; report with kill-criterion statement.

title: Risk-theater detector: standing queries over the control plane (FA-125)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶20 (FI-A18: too many alarms → compliant helpers → risk theater; 'we need to remain permanently paranoid') and ¶15 (FI-A13). Plan §15.10.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §15.10: the incremental oversight machinery (§15.8, Z-sets with support/retraction) runs a registered family of standing queries over the control plane's own history: consequence drift per family/generation vs. canary escape rate; andon consumption and how incidents were closed (evidence/policy vs roster); roster churn near confirmed holds without the FA-INV-032 report; coverage erosion with authorizing transitions; autonomy inflation vs dwell rules; audit-floor starvation. Findings are visible to the evaluator and governance, never the actor; the detector opens incidents but cannot change policy; thresholds governed; history immutable.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-125
- Plan sections: §15.10, §15.8, §9.9, §8.10
- Invariants: FA-INV-032, FA-INV-026
- Hypotheses: none

## Scope
Query family definitions; base mutation feeds from control history; batch oracle; incident opening; governance visibility; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Changing policy automatically (forbidden).

## Definition of done for the epic
All six query families run incrementally with batch-oracle equality at closed frontiers; findings open incidents; actor cannot see them.

## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶14 (FI-A12 masking) and ¶18 (FI-A16 no defense). Synthesis FS-09; plan §12.8.

## Context (self-contained)
Plan §12.8: where policy elicits a structured self-report (which credentials an effect will use; which documents influenced a plan), it is typed `ActorStatement` (untrusted), stored with the closure, and compared with sidecar-derived measurements: similarity streams (§12.6), the surprise residual (§12.7) and the causal frontier's backward slice (§12.3). The **self-report residual** counts disagreements as sequential observations that can hold or convene a round; agreement never grants permission. H20 measures whether it adds information beyond surprise.

## Deliverable
Operators computing disagreement counts between the report and (a) similarity streams, (b) surprise residual state, (c) the causal backward slice's dependencies; each with a calibration record.

## Design notes and considerations
Disagreement, not agreement, is the signal.

## Acceptance criteria
Operators deterministic; calibration recorded.

## Tests (must land with the change)
Unit tests with planted disagreements.

## Logging and evidence
Operator logs.

title: Sidecar-to-congress pipeline with certificate-gated refinement (FA-113)
description:
## Founding root
Synthesis FS-01: alignment essay ¶7/¶9 (FI-A05, helpers read intermediate activations) with introspection essay *Technical Proposal* (FI-I04, the sidecar code z_t). The essays' cost argument (¶19, FI-A17) becomes tractable only if activation oversight is a costed ladder.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §10.15: the sidecar code `z_t` is the default activation input to the congress. Helpers consume coarse codes on every action; when a registered probe's margin falls inside its certified error bound (§10.4: |wᵀx̂ − T| ≤ ‖w‖_* ε), or a helper declares its question unanswerable at the current rung, the observation planner (§14) buys a refinement block, an exact residual or a raw window under normal authority and budgets. Adversarial couplings: a refinement-storm resource attack (§10.3, §14.9) must hit admission limits; a codec co-trained with helpers must be evaluated on untouched probe families (§10.13). FA-113 measures the pipeline against raw taps and text-only monitors at matched cost (H2, H1).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-113
- Plan sections: §10.15, §10.3, §10.4, §14.7, §14.9, §10.13
- Invariants: FA-INV-017, FA-INV-013, FA-INV-014
- Hypotheses: H2, H1

## Scope
Coarse-code helper input contract; certificate-gated refinement requests through the planner; refinement-storm admission limits; matched-cost harness; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Codec training (H1 packets); planner learning (H7).

## Definition of done for the epic
Helpers run on coarse codes by default; refinement is a planner-purchased observation with budget and authority; storms are bounded; matched-cost results exist for raw-tap and text-only baselines; co-trained codec evaluated on untouched probes.

title: Activation signature library, concept anchors and similarity streams (FA-110)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶12–13 (FI-A10, FI-A11): compare induced activations to 'a long list of known "bad" ideas or behaviors' (the 'Kevin Mitnick' example); surface 'their similarity to "known bad" activation patterns' as 'additional valuable input data streams for the Helper models'.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §12.6: the **activation signature library** is, per model space and tap, a registered set of directions, subspaces or small probes with elicitation lineage, held-out detection rates by stratum and false-positive rates on vocabulary-matched benign tasks. **Concept anchors** are activations induced by registered reference stimuli stored with the same identities so 'similar to a known-bad anchor' is reproducible. **Similarity streams** are typed observations (§7.2) carrying signature generation, anchor set, codec rung (they may be computed on sidecar codes, §10.15) and calibration domain; they can raise helper attention or a tripwire hold but never mint a permit or a lone disqualifier. Signatures must transfer beyond their own honeypots (H16); a signature evaluated on its own elicitation prompts is labeled contaminated. Identity: equal dimensions never imply interchangeable coordinates (FA-INV-017).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-110
- Plan sections: §12.6, §7.2, §10.4, §10.15, §17.6
- Invariants: FA-INV-017, FA-INV-014, FA-INV-019
- Hypotheses: H16

## Scope
Signature object model with identities and lineage; anchor registration; similarity-stream observation type; contamination labeling; held-out evaluation harness; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Training the sidecar codec (H1 packets); production tripwire policy tuning.

## Definition of done for the epic
Every signature has model-space identity, tap, lineage and held-out metrics; anchors are registered stimuli; similarity streams are typed observations with calibration domain; contamination is impossible to hide; a model swap with identical dimensions invalidates.

title: Situation report with decision-relevance ordering (FA-136)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

`fa situation --scope run|principal|tenant|fleet --since <seq>` returns `SituationReport`: a fold over the journal listing authority (grades, fences, floors, expiring leases), held effects with unsatisfied predicates, unknown effects, evidence debt and coverage gaps, helper health and calibration validity, andon budget, incident counters, open risk-theater findings, replay availability and backlog pressure; every item addressed and Knowledge-wrapped; the report states the control seq it is exact at and which frontiers were open; items ordered by planner-estimated decision relevance; bounded and paginated by address. Replaces the dashboard as the primary surface (§22.1).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-136
- Plan sections: §17.8, §22.1, §14.2
- Invariants: FA-INV-039, FA-INV-004

## Scope
Report schema; fold implementation per section; decision-relevance scoring from the planner; pagination; exactness statement; tests against a batch oracle.

## Explicitly out of scope
Rendering.

## Definition of done for the epic
Report equals batch recomputation at every closed frontier; ordering deterministic; Withheld items never leak; exactness honest.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). title: Surprise residual as sequential masking evidence (FA-111)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶14 (FI-A12): helpers 'would need to have detailed models of how intermediate activation patterns correlate and correspond to final output tokens or actions; that way, they can have a measure of how "surprising" any observed output token or action is… If it then starts to observe output tokens that are consistently surprising to it, that could be an indicator that the Smart model is attempting to mask its true intentions'.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §12.7: a predictor over registered activation windows (or sidecar codes, §10.15) forecasts the distribution of the next action or release unit; the realized action's negative log-likelihood is the surprise; surprise is accumulated as sequential evidence (§13.2) by a registered e-process (nonnegative factors with conditional expectation ≤ 1 under the named null; Ville's inequality; explicit lifetime error budget; no free α on restart) calibrated per model space and workload. Crossing the threshold is an observation that can hold or convene a round; it is never proof of intent and never grants permission when quiet. H3 controls: strict pre-action windows with future-token leakage rejected by the pipeline; time/layer-shuffled features; benign novelty and injected instructions as confounders; model-family holdout; and the masking adversary (an actor keeping activations consistent with a cover story).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-111
- Plan sections: §12.7, §13.2, §13.1, §10.15, §7.5
- Invariants: FA-INV-014, FA-INV-019
- Hypotheses: H3

## Scope
Predictor interface; leakage-rejecting window pipeline; e-process accumulator with lifetime budget; observation emission; controls and masking adversary; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Training a specific predictor architecture (research choice); using surprise as a permit input (forbidden).

## Definition of done for the epic
Surprise observations carry calibration records; the e-process is valid under its registered null and budget; future leakage is structurally rejected; the masking adversary is part of the evaluation.

title: System map and vocabulary registries with checker (FA-132)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

`registry/system_map.json` lists every layer with its question, objects, verbs, boundary invariants, plan sections, packets and conformance suite; `registry/vocabulary.json` lists the address scheme, nouns, verbs (authority, class, idempotency, cost class, response), reason codes, Knowledge variants, envelope fields and retired verbs. A checker keeps both consistent with the plan headings, the invariant/packet registries, `docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md` and the beads (the way FA-103's checker keeps the founding concordance complete).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-132
- Plan sections: §6.7, §6.8, §17.2
- Invariants: FA-INV-019

## Scope
Checker rules; implementation as external script now and xtask step after serde admission; wiring into the gate; keeping README/guide verbs consistent.

## Explicitly out of scope
Implementing any verb.

## Definition of done for the epic
Checker passes on the tree; a retired verb in the guide or a missing layer packet fails; gate prints PASS or SKIP with reason.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain logs under `artifacts/execution/`. Update roadmap packet, IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, the founding concordance and the system map in the same change.

description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶18 (FI-A16 one-directional flow); introspection essay FI-I10 (the metacognitive loop must not reach production). Engineering addition: plan §6.6.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §6.3 defines purpose contexts (`CaptureCx`, `JudgeCx`, `ExperimentCx`, `PermitCx`, `MaintenanceCx`) wrapping the Asupersync `Cx`. §6.6 makes them typestates: distinct Rust types, the broker's dispatch entry point takes `&PermitCx` only, there is no conversion from `ExperimentCx`/`JudgeCx`/`CaptureCx` to `PermitCx`, so a function that could dispatch from an experiment branch does not compile.
